item.title: Anko Nabe: Ibaraki's Signature Monkfish Hot Pot — Guide
item.description: Anko nabe, monkfish hot pot, is Ibaraki’s signature winter dish, drawing on the abundant monkfish catch landed along the prefecture’s Pacific coast, particularly around Oarai. The dish traditionally uses nearly every part of the fish — liver, skin, and meat simmered together with vegetables and miso in a technique historically performed by hanging the fish and carving it directly, as monkfish’s slippery texture makes it difficult to prepare on a standard cutting board.

item.title: Jappa-jiru: Aomori's Cod & Miso Winter Hotpot — Guide
item.description: Jappa-jiru is a beloved Aomori fisherman’s soup — cod offcuts, miso, daikon, tofu and seasonal vegetables simmered into a deeply savory winter broth. Once a zero-waste dish made on fishing boats, it’s now cherished comfort food at izakayas along the Tsugaru coast from November to March. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Aomori City & Tsugaru coast Hours Izakaya/restaurant hours Admission ~¥600–1,000 a bowl Time needed About 1 hour Best time Winter (Nov–Mar) What to Try Rich cod-and-miso broth with daikon and tofu.

item.title: Senbei-jiru: Hachinohe's Cracker Hotpot — Aomori Guide
item.description: Senbei-jiru is a hearty Hachinohe specialty in which special nambu wheat crackers are simmered in a savory chicken or fish broth until they turn pleasantly chewy. Soul-warming and unusual, it’s a beloved local winter staple and one of Aomori’s most distinctive comfort foods. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachinohe, Aomori Hours Restaurant/izakaya hours Admission ~¥700–1,200 Time needed About 1 hour Best time Winter (warming dish) What to Try Chewy nambu wheat crackers simmered in broth.
